title: Review: Animal tissues organs and organ systems; Plant tissues organs and systems
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.2.2-c35 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.3-c04 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.2-c10 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.2.3-c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.2.2-q19, 4.2.2-q23, 4.2.2-q24, 4.2.3-q07, 4.2.3-q02, 4.2.2-q20, 4.2.2-q22, 4.2.2-q25, 4.2.3-q03, 4.2.2-q21, 4.2.3-q06, 4.2.3-q01. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Risk factor
items.clue: Something that is linked to an increased rate of a disease.

items.label: Meristem tissue
items.clue: Plant tissue found at the growing tips of shoots and roots.

items.label: Lipase
items.clue: An enzyme that breaks down lipids (fats) to glycerol and fatty acids.

items.label: Xylem tissue
items.clue: The tissue that transports water and mineral ions from the roots to the stems and leaves.

options.text: The state of being free of catching diseases.
The state of having no risk factors present.
The state of both physical and mental well-being.
The state of the body when disease is absent.

questions.explanation: Health is the state of physical and mental well-being, so it is more than the absence of disease.

questions.stem: Smoking is described as a risk factor for lung cancer. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A correlation in data proves that it is a cause.
It is a factor linked to an increased rate of disease.
It is the one risk factor for this type of cancer.
It leads to the disease in each person who smokes.

questions.explanation: Risk factors are linked to an increased rate of a disease, and smoking is a lifestyle risk factor for lung disease and lung cancer.

questions.stem: What is happening to the cells in a tumour?

options.text: Changes in cells lead to uncontrolled growth.
The cells in the tissue die and are not replaced.
Benign cells travel around in the bloodstream.
Lifestyle damages the membrane around the cell.

questions.explanation: Cancer is the result of changes in cells that lead to uncontrolled growth and division.

questions.stem: How is the structure of palisade mesophyll related to its function in a leaf?

options.text: Its cells are spread apart to let gases move around
Its cells are hollow tubes made stronger by lignin
Its cells contain many chloroplasts that absorb light
Its cells are one tissue that forms the whole leaf

questions.explanation: Palisade mesophyll cells are packed with chloroplasts near the upper surface of the leaf, so the tissue is structured to absorb light for photosynthesis.

questions.stem: How does a root hair cell take up water and mineral ions from the soil?

options.text: Water enters by osmosis and ions by active transport
Water and mineral ions both enter the cell by osmosis
Water enters by osmosis and sugars by translocation
Water enters through pores in the cells' end walls

questions.explanation: Root hair cells are adapted for the efficient uptake of water by osmosis, and mineral ions by active transport.

questions.stem: Which statement about the interaction of different types of disease is correct?

options.text: Communicable disease has no effect on other illness.
Mental illness is not affected by physical illness.
Cancers are triggered by lifestyle, not by viruses.
An immune reaction to a pathogen can trigger allergies.

questions.explanation: Different types of disease may interact: immune reactions initially caused by a pathogen can trigger allergies such as skin rashes and asthma.

questions.stem: A scientist studies whether a substance is a risk factor using data from 20 people. Why is this a problem?

options.text: A risk factor affects each person in the sample.
The sample size has no effect on the result.
A correlation in the data would prove a cause.
The sample is too small to be representative.

questions.explanation: The principles of sampling applied to epidemiological data require a sample large enough to represent the population before conclusions are drawn.

questions.stem: How do malignant tumour cells differ from benign tumour cells?

options.text: They stay inside a membrane in one part of the body.
They invade tissues and form secondary tumours.
They are caused by lifestyle rather than by genes.
They divide more slowly than normal healthy cells.

questions.explanation: Malignant tumour cells are cancers: they invade neighbouring tissues and spread in the blood to different parts of the body, where they form secondary tumours.

options.text: Water and mineral ions move up to the leaves
Dissolved sugars move to the rest of the plant
Cell sap moves through tubes stiffened by lignin
Water and mineral ions enter cells by osmosis

questions.explanation: Translocation is the movement of food molecules through phloem tissue, carrying dissolved sugars from the leaves to the rest of the plant for immediate use or storage.

questions.stem: A scatter diagram shows a correlation between hours of exercise and heart health. What can be concluded?

options.text: Exercise has been proved to cause good heart health.
People who exercise avoid getting heart disease.
The variables are linked, but no cause is proven.
The sample size does not matter for this result.

questions.explanation: A scatter diagram can be used to identify a correlation between two variables, but a causal mechanism has been proven for some risk factors and not for others.

questions.stem: A student measured the water lost by three identical shoots. Shoot A lost 1.2 cm3 in 60 minutes in still air at 20 degrees C. Shoot B lost 2.4 cm3 in 60 minutes in moving air at 20 degrees C. Shoot C lost 2.0 cm3 in 40 minutes in still air at 30 degrees C. Which conclusion do the results support?

options.text: The highest rate of water loss was in moving air at 20 C
The lowest rate of water loss was in moving air at 20 C
The highest rate of water loss was in still air at 30 C
Still air at 20 C gave the highest rate of water loss

questions.explanation: Rate of transpiration is volume divided by time: shoot C lost 2.0 cm3 in 40 minutes, which is 0.05 cm3 per minute, higher than shoot B at 0.04 and shoot A at 0.02.

questions.stem: What does xylem tissue transport, and in which direction?

options.text: Dissolved sugars, from the leaves to all parts
Water and mineral ions, from the roots to leaves
Cell sap, from each living cell to the next one
Mineral ions, drawn into the roots by osmosis

questions.explanation: Xylem tissue transports water and mineral ions from the roots to the stems and leaves, carrying the water in the transpiration stream.
